column4: Same as Ignite (does not require a torch)
column6: MATCHES. Writes 0x96 (150) into DS:26, the dungeon light counter, with no darkness precondition, and always spends. asm/3139, filmed twice.

column4: Transport to the same spot on the next lower floor if the square behind your destination is open
column6: MATCHES, including the odd clause. The gate is asm/1451 testing DS:23/DS:24 on the candidate floor for exactly zero, and DS:23/DS:24 is player minus facing, so "behind" is literal and relative to facing. Measured three ways in one session.

column4: Transport to the same spot on the next higher floor if the square behind your destination is open
column6: MATCHES, plus an undocumented clause: at floor 0 the arm branches into the SURFACE tail and exits the site to the world map.

column4: Remove the wall immediately in front of you (does not work on outer edge walls)
column6: PARTLY. The removal is proven: facing a rock cell, (4,5) went 0x80 -> 0x00 with the charge spent. The outer-edge exclusion was NOT tested. Unresolved: one opened cell read 0x01 rather than 0x00, so clear-bit versus zero-byte is not settled.

column4: Immediately exit the current dungeon or tower
column6: MATCHES, and depth is irrelevant: cast from floor 1 it returned the player to the world cell entered by, not a cell derived from the cast position.

column4: 50% chance to destroy the enemy in front of you
column6: MATCHES, and now with a mechanism. The arm is call rand_byte ; js FAILED ; jmp the KILL target, so it is KILL behind a coin flip. The flip is bit 7 of the generator's new byte, measured at 50.0% of 200000 simulated draws from a live state. asm/3139 previously recorded this claim as NOT FOUND; that is retracted.

column4: Deals 31 + twice your level damage to an enemy in front of you
column6: SHAPE MATCHES, INPUT DOES NOT. The amount is 2*DS:56 + 0x1e + 1, so 31 + 2x is right as arithmetic, but DS:56 is the high BCD byte of experience, not a level, and doubling a BCD digit is not monotone: DS:56 = 0x99 yields 82 damage and 0x01 yields 33. Measured at both points.

column4: Teleports you to a random spot on the current floor (successful only if spot is open)
column6: MATCHES EXACTLY. Two rand_byte draws, each and $0xf or $0x1 (random odd 1..15), written to DS:23/DS:24, gated by the same asm/1451 validity call the ladders use, then copied over the player position. Both exits filmed in a dungeon: (2,11) -> (7,1).

column4: Destroys the enemy in front of you (always succeeds)
column6: MATCHES. No dice in front of the shared target scan; two casts, two kills, no refusal. The award pays out from the victim's own entry.

column1: # NOT ESTABLISHED BY THIS TABLE
# The price column is unverified and is the interesting disagreement. asm/20AB_bcd_price_from_stats
# derives a BCD quote from the caller's index and the bit length of [DS:50] + [DS:4E] (int plus
# charisma), so a fixed per-spell cost cannot exist and a high-int buyer is quoted less for the
# same spell. A maxout character (int 99, cha 99) should therefore be quoted BELOW these numbers.
# Nobody has quoted a spell shoppe live. That is the open test.
